prerequisites: Knowledge on fundamental aspects concerning the most common engineering materials, technical drawings and stress and strain states.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire advanced knowledge on the processes required to transform raw material into finished products with market value, through processes carried out on machines or systems.

Integrate notions acquired in metallurgy, machine design, and mechanical drawing to enrich knowledge and operational capabilities in mechanical manufacturing processes, gaining awareness of the wider multidisciplinary context of engineering.

Determine the method of carrying out the main manufacturing processes to address advanced design themes, even of considerable complexity, and treat the innovation and development of new products and processes.
Appropriately choose the process able to produce the product with the design specifications.
Evaluate the effect of process parameters on product costs and properties.
Improve the degree of independent judgment.

syllabus_topics: INTRODUCTION. Definitions, the product life cycle, main manufacturing processes, relationship between processes and materials, main process characteristics, elements involved in the implementation of a process.
METAL CASTING. Fundamentals of casting and classification, mold, pattern, core, undercut, pouring of the molten metal, cooling effects, castability.
Expendable mold casting processes: sand casting and mold making, other expendable mold casting processes.
Permanent mold casting processes: the basic permanent-mold process, die casting (cold-chamber and hot-chamber die casting).
METAL FORMING. Fundamentals of plasticity, constitutive models, tension test, axysimmetric compression test, friction, strain energy method, workability, classification of metal working processes.

Forging: definitions, forgiability, forging machines, factors affecting the die filling, flashing, open die forging, close die forging and other related processes, flash formation, preforming, forging forces.
Sheet forming: anisotropy and formability of sheet metals.
Sheet bending: V bending, elastic springback, bending force.
Deep drawing of axysimmetric parts: engineering analysis, choice of process parameters, calculation of the blank diameter.
Deep drawing of non axsimmetric parts and sheet stamping.

MATERIAL REMOVAL PROCESSES. Definitions, cutting and feed motions, cutting parameters, cutting time, material removal rate, theory of chip formation in metal machining, actual chip formation, types of chip, build up edge, cutting forces, specific energy, thermal aspects in cutting, threedimensional cutting, machinability, tool wear and tool life, Taylor tool life, cutting tool technology:
Machining operations: turning, drilling, reaming, milling and grinding.
assessment_rules: The evaluation is based on an oral exam where the student must answer four questions chosen among the course topics. The four questions have the same weight in the final grade. A minimum score of eighteen points is achieved by demonstrating sufficient capacity to answer all questions. The maximum grade, thirty points with honors, is awarded for full mastery of topics, exposed autonomously and with appropriate technical language.
